# `aitbc system file-info`

Show file metadata without dumping content — the safe form of `system file`. Reports size, mtime, owner, mode and type; for JSON files also the top-level key names. ``--field`` prints a single scalar field and hard-refuses denied names: any token (split on ``_``/``-``/camelCase) in pass/password/passwd/pwd/passphrase/secret/token/key/keys/private/ credential/credentials/auth/signing/mnemonic/seed/dsn/url/uri; the separator-insensitive forms privatekey, apikey, secretkey, passphrase, passwd, credential and credentials; any name ending in ``key`` whose prefix is private/secret/api/auth/signing/access — including inside nested objects — names ending in ``_url``/``_uri``/``_dsn``; secret-shaped values (user:pass URLs, 0x+64-hex, 40+-char hex/base64 runs, three-part dotted tokens); and values over 200 characters. Coverage is the ``system file`` allowlist: ``/var/lib/aitbc/wallets`` and ``/etc/aitbc/credentials`` are inside it; ``/root/.aitbc/wallets`` is not — the path refuses before anything is read.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc system file-info [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--path` | text | — | yes | Absolute path under /opt/aitbc, /etc/aitbc, /etc/systemd, /var/log/aitbc, or /var/lib/aitbc |
| `--field` | text | — | no | Print one scalar top-level JSON field (e.g. address) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc system file-info --path <path>
```
